Royal Rumble 01 – New Orleans, LA – Arena – January 21, 2001 (announced at 17,137; 16,056; sell out)
Sunday Night Heat – live – hosted by Michael Cole & Tazz; featured a video package recapping the feud between Chris Jericho and WWF IC Champion Chris Benoit to hype their ladder match later in the night; included Lilian Garcia conducting an interview with Benoit, arriving to the arena, about his upcoming title defense; featured a promo by WWF Tag Team Champions Edge & Christian in the aisle regarding their upcoming title defense against the Dudley Boyz, during which they had clips shown on the big screen of their midget Dudley Boyz saying “Wazzzzup!” and “Testify!” after each point the champions made; included pre-taped comments from fans outside the arena as to who they thought would win the Royal Rumble match; included the announcement that applications were available for WWF Tough Enough on MTV; featured a video package recapping the feud between Chyna and WWF Women’s Champion Ivory; included a promo in the aisle by Val Venis, Steven Richards, the Goodfather, Bull Buchanon, & Ivory regarding their participation in the show; featured a backstage segment in which the Undertaker was shown driving his motorcycle; included footage of WWF World Champion Kurt Angle appearing the previous Friday in Washington DC as part of George W. Bush’s inaguration, where he represented the Smackdown Your Vote campaign; featured a video package recapping the recent history between Triple H and Angle; included Garcia conducting a backstage interview with Angle regarding his upcoming title defense against Triple H, during which Trish joined Angle; featured a backstage segment showing the Rock arriving to the arena; included footage from earlier in the night of Drew Carey arriving to the arena; featured Cole conducting a backstage interview with Vince McMahon regarding the altercation between Triple H and Austin on Smackdown and whether that would cost Triple H his world title shot and Austin his spot in the Rumble match, with McMahon saying he would not take their opportunities away; Cole then asked about surprises in store for the Rumble match, with McMahon walking off without answering:
D-Lo Brown & Chaz (w/ Tiger Ali Singh) defeated Taka Michinoku & Sho Funaki at 1:51 when Chaz pinned Funaki following a modified powerbomb; prior to the bout, Taka & Funaki cut a promo in the aisle – voiced over by Shane McMahon & the Undertaker – regarding their opponents; stipulations stated one of the winning team would compete in the Royal Rumble match (Royal Rumble 01)
Pay-per-view bouts – included Jim Ross & Jerry Lawler on commentary; featured footage from Sunday Night Heat of Drew Carey arriving to the arena; included footage of Michael Cole conducting a backstage interview with Vince McMahon in which he said Steve Austin would compete in the Royal Rumble and Triple H would challenge for the WWF World Title, as scheduled, despite their altercation earlier in the week; featured a backstage segment with Triple H & Stephanie McMahon in which they discussed Triple H’s match against Kurt Angle; moments later, Carey came in, met Stephanie, and joked that he saw Kamala singing at the airport; Carey then said he was trying to find Vince to talk about his upcoming pay-per-view special “Drew Carey’s Improv All Stars”, with Stephanie telling Drew that Trish Stratus wanted to meet him as well; included a backstage segment showing Farooq & Bradshaw playing cards before showing each other their spots in the Royal Rumble match; Crash Holly then walked in and said, despite them being friends, he would have to throw them out of the ring in the Rumble; featured a backstage segment with Trish and Carey in which she tried to get him out of her room by saying she was involved with someone; moments later, Vince walked in and, after discussing Carey’s upcoming improv show, suggested Carey take part in the Rumble match later in the show; included a backstage segment with Chyna and Billy Gunn in which Gunn tried to talk her out of her upcoming match against WWF Women’s Champion Ivory because of her condition, with Chyna saying there was nothing that would stop her; featured Cole conducting a backstage segment with WWF IC Champion Chris Jericho regarding his title win in the ladder match; included a backstage segment in which Stephanie went looking for the makeup artist and found Trish, with the two arguing about the upcoming Triple H vs. Angle match; featured a backstage segment in which Harvey Wippleman gave Carey his gear for his upcoming match; moments later, Kane walked in and then walked out after Carey introduced himself to him; included a backstage segment with Tiger Ali Singh, D-Lo Brown & Chaz in which D-Lo and Chaz argued over which of them would compete in the Rumble match; moments later, Vince walked in and said neither would be in the match and they had been replaced; Singh then asked what great superstar would fill that spot, with Vince saying Carey; featured pre-taped comments from fans at WWF New York about who they thought would win the Triple H vs. Angle match, with the fans largely divided; included a backstage segment showing Rikishi, at #30, and the Undertaker in the respective locker rooms preparing for the Rumble match; featured Kevin Kelly conducting a backstage interview with the Rock regarding his participation in the Rumble match:
The Dudley Boyz defeated WWF Tag Team Champions Edge & Christian to win the titles at 10:00 when D-Von pinned Edge following the 3D after a failed Wazzup Drop by the champions
Chris Jericho defeated WWF IC Champion Chris Benoit in a ladder match to win the title at 18:44 after knocking Benoit off the top of the ladder, with the champion hitting the top rope and bouncing off to the floor (The Ladder Match)
WWF Women’s Champion Ivory (w/ Steven Richards) pinned Chyna at 3:28 after the challenger seemingly aggrevated a neck injury after hitting a springboard elbow in the corner; after the bout, Jerry Lawler left the broadcast table to check on her, along with Billy Gunn, road agents Tony Garea, Sgt. Slaughter, and medics; moments later, Chyna was taken backstage on a stretcher and loaded into an ambulance (Divas in Hedonism)
WWF World Champion Kurt Angle pinned Triple H at 24:15 when, as referee Earl Hebner was knocked out on the floor, Steve Austin came out, assaulted the challenger around ringside, and hit him with the title belt; moments later, after Austin rolled a dazed Hebner into the ring, Austin climbed back into the ring and dropped Triple H with the Stunner before leaving the ring and Angle making the cover; prior to the contest, Stephanie McMahon escorted Triple H to the ring and Trish Stratus escorted but both women were taken backstage by Vince McMahon at around the 15-minute mark when they began fighting each other around ringside
Steve Austin won the 30-man Royal Rumble match at 1:01:51 by last eliminating Kane with a clothesline following several chair shots to the head; Order of entry: Jeff Hardy (0:00), Bull Buchanon (0:00), Matt Hardy (1:50), Farooq (3:36), Drew Carey (6:12), Kane (8:09), WWF Hardcore Champion Raven (8:53), Al Snow (10:33); Snow ran out before his time and attacked Raven on the floor; he was held back by referee Teddy Long until the entrant time was official, Perry Saturn (escorted to the ring by Terri) (12:53), Steve Blackman (14:23), Grandmaster Sexay (16:12), the Honkytonk Man (18:36), the Rock (20:23), the Goodfather (22:09), Tazz (23:51), Bradshaw (25:49), Albert (27:39), Hardcore Holly (29:29), K-Kwick (31:25), Val Venis (33:16), WWF European Champion William Regal (35:12), Test (37:03), the Big Show (39:02), Crash Holly (40:59), the Undertaker (43:03), Scotty 2 Hotty (44:58), Steve Austin (52:13); Austin was attacked from behind by Triple H in the aisle before he entered the ring, assaulted near the entranceway and bloodied until referees could send Triple H backstage, thus he entered the ring several minutes after he came out; Billy Gunn (47:57); Haku (49:50) (Haku’s surprise return after a 9-year absence), and Rikishi (52:12)
Order of elimination: Buchanon by the Hardys via a double clothesline (2:08); Farooq by the Hardys after sustaining the Twist of Fate / Swanton combo (4:34); the Hardys eliminated each other while fighting on the top rope (Jeff – 6:35, Matt – 6:36); Carey eliminated himself as Kane fought with Raven (9:06); Sexay by Kane after hitting him in the head with a trash can (17:16); Blackman by Kane after being hit in the head with a trash can lid as he attempted to skin the cat (17:33); Snow by Kane (17:42); Raven by Kane (17:45); Saturn by Kane (17:57); Honky by Kane after smashing his own guitar over his head (19:53); the Goodfather by Rock via a punch (22:25); Tazz by Kane after being punched off the top rope (24:01); Regal by Test (37:13); Test by Show via a clothesline (39:12); Kwick by Show via a press slam (39:19); Show by Rock via a clothesline (40:26); after the elimination, Show attacked Rock on the floor and dropped him with a chokeslam through the announce table; Bradshaw by Taker (43:27); Crash by Kane (43:29); Albert by Kane via a clothesline (43:32); Hardcore by Taker (43:33); Venis by Taker (43:38); Scotty by Taker & Kane via a double clothesline after a double chokeslam (45:44); Haku by Austin via a clothesline (52:42); Taker by Rikishi via a kick to the face (53:54); Rikishi by Rock via knocking him off the top rope after landing a low blow to avoid the Bonzai Drop (55:00); Gunn by Austin (55:24); Rock by Kane as Rock attempted to eliminate Austin (58:45); Kane by Austin

Smackdown! – included Vince McMahon cutting an in-ring promo to begin the show in which he said that the Rock would face the Big Show later in the show to determine the #1 contender for the world title at No Way Out; he went on to state that Triple H and Steve Austin would have wrestlers representing them in a match, where if Austin or Triple H had the winning wrestler, they would be able to pick the stipulations for their bout at No Way Out; after asking for a volunteer to come out and pick at random the wrestlers who would be competing on behalf of Austin and Triple H, William Regal and Trish Stratus came out, with Trish picking Billy Gunn to represent Steve Austin and WWF IC Champion Chris Jericho to represent Triple H; later in the show, Triple H found Gunn backstage and asked him to lay down and let Jericho beat him; after Gunn refused, Triple H hit him in the back of the head with a fire extinguisher; Vince McMahon later announced that the match would be changed to Triple H vs. Jericho instead and, on Raw, Rikishi would represent Steve Austin in a match against the Rock, who would represent Triple H; featured a video recap of the first week of the XFL; included a backstage segment in which Kurt Angle and Essa Rios had an altercation, with a match between the two announced to take place on Sunday Night Heat:

Al Snow defeated WWF Hardcore Champion Hardcore Holly to win the title after hitting him with Head
Raven pinned WWF Hardcore Champion Al Snow to win the title after a masked woman interfered on Raven’s behalf
WWF Tag Team Champions the Dudley Boyz defeated the Goodfather & Bull Buchanon following the 3D on Buchanon
The Big Show defeated Billy Gunn
Steve Austin, the Undertaker, the Rock, & Kane defeated Triple H, Chris Benoit, Rikishi, & Haku when the Rock pinned Benoit with the Rock Bottom

WWF @ East Rutherford, NJ – Continental Airlines Arena – February 12, 2001 (15,345; sell out)
Scott Vick defeated Judas Young
Judas Young defeated Tony DeVito
Jakked:
The Goodfather & Bull Buchanon defeated Taka Michinoku & Sho Funaki
Crash Holly pinned Low-Ki with a tornado bulldog
K-Kwick defeated the Inferno Kid
Albert defeated Mike Bell
Raw is War:
WWF IC Champion Chris Jericho defeated Eddie Guerrero via submission with the Walls of Jericho after blocking a hurricanrana; after the bout, X-Pac attacked the champion
Lita, Matt & Jeff Hardy defeated Chris Benoit, Perry Saturn, & Terri when Lita pinned Terri with the Twist of Fate / moonsault combo; after the bout, Dean Malenko helped Lita to her feet before hitting a clothesline on her
The Undertaker & Kane fought Edge & Christian to a no contest when both teams began brawling with the Dudley Boyz, who did guest commentary for the match; the winners of the contest would have become the #1 contenders to the tag team titles
Triple H (w/ Stephanie McMahon) pinned Billy Gunn with the Pedigree after avoiding the Fameasser
X-Pac pinned Grandmaster Sexay with a kick to the midsection and X-Factor; X-Pac’s original opponent was Scotty 2 Hotty but Scotty injured his foot during the match – resulting in X-Pac challenging his partner; after the match, Chris Jericho attacked X-Pac until Justin Credible made the save (Credible’s debut)
WWF World Champion Kurt Angle & WWF Hardcore Champion Raven defeated the Big Show & Essa Rios when Raven pinned Rios following Angle’s Olympic Slam; after the match, the masked woman aided Raven in attacking the Big Show until Show fought back by hitting the chokeslam on Raven as Angle ran backstage
The Rock (w/ Triple H & Stephanie McMahon) pinned Rikishi (w/ Steve Austin) with the Rock Bottom; after the match, Rikishi and Triple H double teamed the Rock until Austin hit the Stunner on Rikishi and had a face off with Triple H; due to prematch stipulations, Triple H earned the right to choose the stipulations for his match with Austin at No Way Out

WWF @ Long Island, NY – Nassau Coliseum – February 13, 2001 (12,127; sell out)
Scott Vick pinned Steve Bradley with the Kryptonite Krunch
The Inferno Kid pinned Mike Bell
Smackdown! – 2/15/01:
Kane (w/ the Undertaker) pinned Edge (w/ Christian) with a flying clothesline; after the match, the Dudley Boyz – who were watching from ringside – taunted Kane until he stood on the ring apron while, in the ring, Christian Irish whipped Taker into Kane who then went through a table that had been set up by the Dudleys; moments thereafter, Kane and the Undertaker hit chokeslams on Edge and Christian
Matt Hardy (w/ Lita & Jeff Hardy) pinned Perry Saturn (w/ Terri) with a roll up after Lita was knocked into the arms of Dean Malenko – who had just came to ringside; after the match, Malenko kissed Lita before she slapped him and challenged him to a match the following Monday on Raw
Steve Austin pinned Chris Benoit with the Stunner
X-Pac defeated WWF IC Champion Chris Jericho via disqualification when Eddie Guerrero prevented the pinfall from being made after the challenger hit the X-Factor; after the bout, Guerrero and Jericho began brawling until Justin Credible appeared and nailed Guerrero; moments thereafter, Jericho chased Credible and X-Pac off with a steel chair before hitting Guerrero with the chair
WWF Hardcore Champion Raven fought the Big Show to a no contest when Raven ran away with help from the masked woman after Taka Michinoku, Sho Funaki, Albert, K-Kwick, Val Venis, Tazz, Hardcore Holly and Steve Blackman got involved in the match
The Rock defeated Triple H via disqualification when Kurt Angle prevented the Rock?s pin attempt; after the match, a brawl ensued involving the Rock, Triple H, Angle, Chris Benoit, and Steve Austin; as the show went off the air, the Rock was caught in Angle?s ankle lock while Austin was caught in Benoit?s Crippler Crossface as Triple H poured beer on him
Sunday Night Heat – 2/18/01:
Haku defeated Hardcore Holly with the Tongan Death Grip
Eddie Guerrero pinned K-Kwick with the Frog Splash
The Undertaker defeated Christian (w/ Edge) via disqualification when Edge prevented the pinfall by hitting Taker with a steel chair after Taker hit the powerbomb on Christian; after the bout, Kane made the save

WWF @ Cedar Falls, IA – UNI-Dome – February 17, 2001 (5,493)
Steve Blackman pinned WWF Hardcore Champion Raven to win the title after hitting him with a kendo stick
Raven pinned WWF Hardcore Champion Steve Blackman to win the title with a roll up as Blackman prepared to leave ringside
Hardcore & Molly Holly defeated Steven Richards & WWF Women’s Champion Ivory when Molly pinned Ivory with a flying bodypress
Chris Benoit defeated X-Pac via submission with the Crippler Crossface
WWF Tag Team Champions the Dudley Boyz defeated Edge & Christian, Matt & Jeff Hardy, and Bull Buchanon & the Goodfather following the 3D
WWF World Champion Kurt Angle (w/ Trish Stratus) pinned WWF IC Champion Chris Jericho with the Olympic Slam
WWF European Champion Test pinned Val Venis with the pumphandle slam
The Acolytes defeated the Big Bossman & Albert following a reverse DDT
The Big Show pinned K-Kwick (sub. for Billy Gunn) with the chokeslam
Steve Austin, Kane, & the Undertaker defeated Triple H, Rikishi, & Haku when the Undertaker pinned Haku with a chokeslam

WWF @ Evansville, IN – February 18, 2001 (7,321)
Too Cool defeated Taka Michinoku & Sho Funaki
The Kat pinned Victoria after a Bronko Buster
Jerry Lawler pinned WWF Light Heavyweight Champion Dean Malenko in a non-title match after Lita interfered
Chris Benoit defeated X-Pac via submission with the Crippler Crossface
Steve Austin, Kane, & the Undertaker defeated Triple H, Rikishi, & Haku when Kane pinned Haku with the chokeslam
Charlie & Russ Haas defeated Scott Vick & Steve Bradley with an inside cradle after faking an injury
K-Kwick defeated Justin Credible
Eddie Guerrero pinned Bo Dupp (sub. for Al Snow) with the frogsplash
Matt & Jeff Hardy defeated Edge & Christian when Jeff scored the pin with the Swanton

WWF @ Cape Girardeau, MO – Show Me Center – February 18, 2001 (4,259)
Hardcore Holly defeated Steven Richards
Crash Holly defeated the Brooklyn Brawler
Steve Blackman pinned WWF Hardcore Champion Raven to win the title
Raven pinned WWF Hardcore Champion Steve Blackman to win the title after a masked woman interfered
The Acolytes defeated the Big Bossman & Albert
WWF Tag Team Champions the Dudley Boyz defeated the Goodfather & Bull Buchanon
WWF European Champion Test defeated Val Venis
The Big Show defeated Al Snow
WWF World Champion Kurt Angle defeated WWF IC Champion Chris Jericho

WWF @ St. Louis, MO – Savvis Center – February 19, 2001 (14,840; sell out)
Charlie & Russ Haas defeated Steve Bradley & Scott Vick
Bo Dupp defeated Drill Instructor
Jakked:
WWF European Champion Test defeated Essa Rios in a non-title match
K-Kwick defeated Derrick Stone
Perry Saturn defeated James Grizzle
Taka Michinoku & Sho Funaki defeated Matt Murphy & Steve Thunder
Raw is War:
The Undertaker defeated Christian and WWF Tag Team Champion D-Von Dudley by pinning Christian
Lita pinned Dean Malenko at 3:04 after Matt Hardy interfered as the referee was knocked out, stole away Malenko’s steel chair and hit Malenko with it; after the bout, Hardy kissed Lita, then apologized and walked up the ramp; moments later, she followed and kissed him back on the ramp (Lita: It Just Feels Right)
Eddie Guerrero fought X-Pac to a no contest; Chris Jericho was the guest referee
Rikishi & Haku defeated Matt & Jeff Hardy
WWF Hardcore Champion Raven fought Crash Holly to a no contest
The Rock & Steve Austin defeated WWF World Champion Kurt Angle & Chris Benoit when Rock pinned Benoit

WWF @ Kansas City, MO – Kemper Arena – February 20, 2001
Scott Vick & Steve Bradley defeated Charlie & Russ Haas
Rhino defeated Bo Dupp
Sunday Night Heat – only shown internationally:
Bull Buchanon & the Goodfather defeated Taka Michinoku & Sho Funaki
Tazz defeated Essa Rios
Justin Credible defeated Matt Murphy
WWF Light Heavyweight Champion Dean Malenko defeated Grandmaster Sexay
Smackdown! – included an in-ring interview where Jim Ross was scheduled to interview Steve Austin, but Triple H came out instead and hit the Pedigree on Ross before Steve Austin made the save; featured Jerry Lawler’s final appearance as a commentator on Smackdown! until the 11/20/01 taping:
Rikishi pinned Jeff Hardy (w/ Lita) with the Bonzai Drop; after the match, Rikishi gave Lita the Stinkface until Matt Hardy came to ringside
The Big Show defeated Crash Holly, Perry Saturn (w/ Terri), Steve Blackman, Hardcore Holly, & K-Kwick in a hardcore match by pinning Kwick with the chokeslam; after the match, Raven – who was doing guest commentary – came in the ring and hit Show with a stop sign, but Show fought him off; due to pre-match stipulations, Show became the # 1 contender for the Hardcore title at No Way Out
Chris Benoit & Eddie Guerrero defeated WWF IC Champion Chris Jericho & X-Pac when Jericho submitted to Benoit’s Crippler Crossface after X-Pac kicked Jericho in the face; after the match, X-Pac and Justin Credible attacked Guerrero & Benoit, leaving both laying in the ring
WWF Women’s Champion Ivory fought the Kat to a no contest when Right To Censor came to the ring after Kat removed Ivory’s shirt; after the match, Jerry Lawler was about to enter the ring until he was given the superkick by Steven Richards (who was dressed as security); Lawler was then thrown into the ring and beaten down by RTC, with Richards finishing him off with he DDT on a chair (Kat?s last match in the WWF)
WWF European Champion Test pinned William Regal with the big boot after Al Snow – who was at ringside campaigning to be the Commissioner of the WWF – hit Regal with Head
WWF World Champion Kurt Angle, Edge, & Christian defeated the Rock, the Undertaker, & Kane in a No DQ Match when Angle pinned Rock with the Olympic Slam through a table – originally put into the ring by the Dudley Boyz; after the bout, Angle put Rock in the ankle lock, with Rock tapping as the show went off air
